text: and not co-infected with Lyme dis- ease; the dose is 4 mg/kg daily in two divided doses and should be given for at least 3 days after the patient has be- come afebrile (a total of about 5 to 10 days). Successful treatment of HGA with rifampicin has been reported in pregnancy (gestational age of 10 to 36 weeks)8 and in 2 children with non-life-threatening infection.9 The IDSA7 recommends that patients with mild disease who cannot be given a tetracycline may be given rifampicin 300 mg twice daily for 7 to 10 days; children may be given 10 mg/kg twice daily. Antibacterial susceptibility testing has sug- gested that rifamycins and fluoroquinolones are promising alternatives in the treatment of HGA.10 1. Paddock CD, Childs JE.
